Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.

Registered Republican candidate for United States Senator, Alaska · Challenger

Retired elementary school teacher; former U.S. Forest Service employee

Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. is a Republican from Petersburg, Alaska, who worked for the U.S. Forest Service for 15 years and later taught elementary school. In June 2026 the Alaska Division of Elections disqualified him from the ballot, saying his candidacy was not in good faith, but a Superior Court judge overturned that decision and the Alaska Supreme Court later allowed him on the ballot. He finished third in the August 18 nonpartisan top-four primary with about 2.5% of the vote and chose not to withdraw before the deadline.

Where Jr. stands

Iran / foreign policy
Calls the U.S. war with Iran "ill-conceived" and contrasts his view with the incumbent senator's support for the war.
Energy and cost of living
Names lowering the cost of living, affordable housing and better access to healthcare as his top issues, citing what he has seen while living in Petersburg.
Tariffs / trade
Says tariffs can work if used precisely for specific goals, but argues recent tariffs were applied too broadly, were not effective and raised prices.
Fisheries
Says cuts made by the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) lost scientific data that fisheries programs depend on.
Federal vs. state authority
Supports oversight programs for federal agencies, but says DOGE went too far, cutting too many federal employees, programs and data.
Elections and voting
Supports Alaska's open primary and ranked-choice voting system. Says no one has shown him that widespread voter fraud is a problem.

Background

  • U.S. Forest Service employee, about 15 years
  • Elementary school teacher, Petersburg (retired)
  • Volunteer, Petersburg Volunteer Fire Department
  • Former member of the Alaskan Independence Party; registered Republican since the party dissolved
  • 2026 U.S. Senate primary: third place, about 2.5% of the vote
